newsitem.title: CANADA: Anvil Range had no choice in Yukon shutdown.
newsitem.headline: Anvil Range had no choice in Yukon shutdown.

text.p: Anvil Range Mining Corp had no choice but to temporarily shut down its base metal and silver operations in the Yukon Territories, the company's chief financial officer said Wednesday.
"We were losing, in our judgment, an amount of money that we couldn't sustain in the longer haul," Victor Wells said in an interview.
"If we had kept going, with the low prices and the losses we've sustained in the last couple of months, I don't think we would have lasted."
Mining operations will stop on December 20.
Wells blamed low zinc and lead prices and a stronger Canadian dollar for the company's poor fortunes.
Investors sliced more than 60 percent off the stock, sending it down C$3.70 to C$2.30 after the announcement, in trading of 1.2 million shares.
Anvil Range will continue to operate its mill on previously stockpiled ore.
"We've got enough to process there for three or four months," Wells said. "If all goes well, we'll generate some profits, we'll generate some cash."
The company will constantly monitor metals prices and foreign exchange rates so that it can reopen its operations when the conditions are right, Wells said.
"We truly believe it's temporary," he said. "Those words were carefully chosen. We think we can ride this through."
Anvil Range would need zinc prices to be at about US$0.50 a pound and lead to be at about US$0.35 a pound to be profitable, Wells added.
He said he did not know when the suspension would show up in the company's results.
